title: Thermal Conductivity: W/(m·K), BTU·in/(h·ft²·°F) and R-value
description: 1 W/(m·K) = 6.933 BTU·in/(h·ft²·°F). Copper is 400 W/(m·K); fibreglass batt is 0.04. Insulation specs mix R-values, k-values and U-values freely.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

reviewer.name: Turbo Unit Converter editorial review
reviewer.credential: verified against NIST SP 811 and category-specific ISO references

hero: k is the material property. R = thickness/k. U = 1/R. Confusing them multiplies heat load estimates by 10.
body: Building science and heat-transfer physics arrived at the same equations through different unit systems. Insulation ratings mix them constantly, and estimating a heat load requires disentangling k, R and U.

> 1 W/(m·K) = 6.9334 BTU·in/(h·ft²·°F) = 0.5778 BTU/(h·ft·°F)
> R-value (US) = thickness (in) / k (BTU·in/(h·ft²·°F)) — units of h·ft²·°F/BTU
> RSI (metric) = thickness (m) / k (W/(m·K)) — units of m²·K/W
> 1 RSI = 5.678 R-value(US)
Copper: 400 W/(m·K). Aluminium: 237. Steel: 50. Concrete: 1.5. Glass: 1.0. Water: 0.6. Fibreglass batt: 0.04. Aerogel: 0.015. Air (still): 0.026.

Wall assembly: 100 mm brick (k = 0.72), 50 mm EPS (k = 0.033), 12.5 mm plaster (k = 0.5). R_total = 0.1/0.72 + 0.05/0.033 + 0.0125/0.5 = 0.139 + 1.515 + 0.025 = 1.679 m²·K/W. U = 1/R = 0.60 W/(m²·K). Miscount EPS as W/(m·K) instead of thickness-normalised and you get a wildly optimistic 0.033 W/(m²·K).
k in W/(m·K). R and U carry thickness and reciprocal. RSI × 5.678 = US R-value.

faqs.q: Is R-19 the same as RSI 3.3?
Why do walls have air films?
faqs.a: Interior and exterior surface films add ~0.17 m²·K/W in still-air conditions — sometimes 15% of the total wall R.
